script: "I am trading my ID tag in for a month, but this 1 shift could be my last.". Title: Last day, last disgruntled voice on the phone (for now) I am literally wrapping up my 2-year stint at the front desk of this hotel. My last shift, last anxious moments – I am trying to stay focused, but honestly, it's been tough saying goodbye to my coworkers and regulars. Only 35 minutes left, and the phone rings. I answer, and it's a woman on the other end, talking a mile a minute. I have no idea what she's saying, so she repeats herself – "Yeah, um, do you guys have...?" I politely ask her to clarify, and all I get is "Pack 'n' Plays?" Now, let me tell you, I was clueless about what that even meant. My coworker had to explain it to me back in the day – basically, it's a crib. Like, just say that? But, okay, I've learned to navigate the kid lingo, (sigh). So, we do have one crib, but it's in use, and I let her know that. The drama ensues – the incredulous inflections, the pause, like I am some kind of hotel magician who's supposed to conjure up a gazillion cribs out of thin air. "You only have ONE????" Um, yes, that's what I said. She tries to be all nice and thanks me before proceeding to yell at someone in the background, "THEY DON'T HAVE ANY!!!?!?!" I hung up, sat there for a second, and my rage just... erupted. I mean, I get it, but honestly, she's taking out her parenting fails on me? Like, she didn't bring a crib, and now she's mad at the hotel staff? I am not the one deciding who gets a crib first – it's first come, first serve. If she didn't bring the necessary gear, that's on her, not me. As I sit here, reflecting on this final phone call, I just want to shake my head. Another disgruntled voice, another angry parent, and another 35 minutes of my shift left.
